---
title: "RLGC, Q2D, and Pi Expansion"
subtitle: "How does one frozen N-conductor extraction become an auditable physical ladder?"
toc-depth: 2
---

**Status:** Human-`ACCEPTED` dev5 implementation; stabilization deferred. The public RLGC contract in
[Component Authoring](../component-authoring.qmd#general-rlgc) remains the
authoritative API. This page fixes the loader and compiler mechanics; it does
not turn one extraction into broadband or convergence evidence.

## Accept one native AEDT grammar

`load_q2d_rlgc()` accepts exactly the AEDT 2024.2 combined `CG, RL` CSV profile.
It reads raw bytes, records their SHA-256 before decoding, then requires strict
UTF-8 with no replacement characters or byte-order mark. CRLF and LF delimit
records; all other content is parsed exactly as written. The first five records
must be, in order:

```text
<setup>:LastAdaptive
Problem Type:  CG, RL
C Units:pF/meter, G Units:mho/meter, R Units:ohm/meter, L Units:nH/meter
Reduce Matrix:  Original
Frequency:  <finite-decimal>GHz
```

`<setup>` is recorded as source evidence. `<finite-decimal>` is parsed once to
a finite positive Float64 GHz value and converted to SI Hz; it is extraction
provenance, not a solve-grid instruction. The loader rejects a missing, extra,
or reordered header record rather than accepting a visually similar export.

After any blank separator, exactly one primary block of each title is required:

```text
Capacitance Matrix
Conductance Matrix
Inductance Matrix
Resistance Matrix
```

Primary blocks occur in that C/G/L/R order. The native supplemental blocks
`Capacitance Matrix Coupling Coefficient` and `Spice Capacitance Matrix` may
appear between them, but can neither replace a primary block nor contribute
values; every other title fails closed. A primary block contains one CSV header whose first
field is empty and whose remaining fields are nonempty, unique native labels;
then exactly one row for every header label, in the same order, with the row
label in the first field and one finite decimal value per column. All four
blocks must use that identical native-label order. Whitespace surrounding CSV
fields is trimmed only to identify labels and numeric tokens; the raw-byte
digest remains the source identity.

The public `conductor_map` is a complete bijection from those native labels to
public conductor names. It relabels the ordered basis but never sorts,
subsets, diagonalizes, or otherwise changes it. `reference_conductor` is the
public name for the omitted reference group; it is not required to occur in the
CSV. The receipt carries raw digest, native labels/order, public labels/order,
five header records, source units, SI frequency, canonical matrices, and
profile ID `aedt_q2d_xy_cross_section_positive_z`.

Calling this loader is a **caller assertion** that the bytes came from the
supported AEDT XY-cross-section profile and that extractor `+z` is line
head-to-tail current. CSV bytes cannot prove that origin, direction, setup
convergence, or any external solver run. The receipt therefore records
`profile_boundary="caller_asserted"`; a caller unable to make that assertion
must use a manual `RLGC` declaration instead.

## Validate matrices without repairing them

The loader converts the four declared per-length units to SCNSim SI Float64
arrays once. Every converted entry must be finite, and all symmetry checks are
bit-exact after that conversion:

$$
M_{ij}=M_{ji},\qquad M\in\{C,G,L,R\}.
$$

For the ordered $N\geq1$ conductor basis it then requires:

- $C$ and $G$ have nonpositive off-diagonals and nonnegative row sums;
- $C$ and $L$ pass an unpivoted Float64 Cholesky factorization;
- the minimum eigenvalue of each symmetric $G$ and $R$ is nonnegative.

No tolerance is applied to symmetry, Maxwell signs, row sums, or the
nonnegative-eigenvalue test. SCNSim does not symmetrize, clip a small negative
entry, project to a positive semidefinite matrix, add a grounding term, or
discard a mutual entry. A failed check is invalid input, not a near-valid
network. The continuum model and the reason these matrices share one ordered
conductor basis are maintained in
[Telegrapher Model: From RLGC Continuum to a Finite LC Ladder](https://github.com/arfiligol/SCQ_Design/blob/main/docs/knowledge/transmission-lines/telegrapher-rlgc-distributed-line.qmd#finite-symmetric-pi-section).

Manual `RLGC` follows the same Float64 matrix validation and receives
`source_kind="manual"`; it may record an unspecified source frequency but
never obtains a Q2D profile claim by similarity.

## Expand exactly one symmetric pi ladder

For a transmission line with bound length $\ell$ and fixed positive integer
`n_sections`, the compiler uses

$$
\Delta x=\ell/n_{\mathrm{sections}}.
$$

It allocates stations `0` through `n_sections` for each conductor in declared
order. Station `0` is the qualified `head` pin and station `n_sections` is the
qualified `tail` pin. Section $s$ connects station $s-1$ to $s$ with the full
ordered series blocks $R\Delta x$ and $L\Delta x$. At each end of every section
it stamps the complete Maxwell shunt blocks

$$
G\Delta x/2,\qquad C\Delta x/2
$$

to Plan ground. Thus an interior station has the sum of its two adjacent
half-shunts; an endpoint has exactly one. Length rebinding recomputes
$\Delta x$ but does not change station count, conductor order, matrix rank, or
pin identity.

The implementation must preserve an explicit station/section record even for
an exact-zero branch. Lowering may omit a zero-valued physical row, but its
matrix value, section index, station attachment, and `omitted_as_zero` evidence
remain in the compile product and terminal receipt. There is no scalar
equivalent for an $N>1$ block and no hidden collapse of mutual C/G/L/R terms.

## Lower one graph faithfully for Direct and HB

The pi graph is backend-neutral. Direct consumes every validated full R/L/G/C
block in the declared basis. HB consumes full C/G and L blocks in that same
basis, but only diagonal $R$: any bitwise nonzero off-diagonal resistance
entry makes an HB request fail during preflight. HB must not drop, diagonalize,
or approximate that entry. This is a capability boundary, not a different
physical Plan.

The parent component, section index, station/conductor identities, bound
values, orientation, and each backend lowering are receipt evidence. Direct
and HB therefore may use distinct realizations while remaining traceable to one
expanded graph.

## Render the whole compiled audit

`CircuitDiagramSpec(representation="compiled")` is a deterministic audit of the
expanded graph, not a Direct/HB diagram or a reduced network. It orders line
components by their compiled component identity, then sections ascending, then
conductors in the declared basis. It shows every station and section, endpoint
attachment, $\Delta x$, conductor/reference identity, head-to-tail orientation,
all series blocks, and both endpoint half-shunts. Interior stations identify
both contributions and their total.

For $N=1$ the audit may use ordinary R/L/G/C symbols; for $N>1$ it keeps
ordered conductor lanes and prints complete matrix-valued blocks. Exact-zero
rows may be visually omitted only when their complete table says
`omitted_as_zero`. Pagination is deterministic and retains continuous station
and section IDs; no view, solver row, partial range, or numerical result is
introduced by rendering.

## Preflight evidence

`run.explain()` recompiles the bound graph and reports the facts above,
including Q2D/manual provenance, validation evidence, station map, zero-row
evidence, and Direct/HB capability. It is pure preflight: it does not launch a
solver, allocate an attempt, write a workspace receipt, or materialize a
numerical Result. It may prepare the package-owned Julia environment when a
real compiler preflight requires it; preparation is not solver or receipt work.
